deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues the previous one. Gauss is reducing his Göttingen observations of the minor planet Juno on 8 April 1815. Juno was measured against two comparison stars, *a and *b, whose positions come from a Lalande zone of 20 April 1796 (epoch 1796.301). The previous page fixed the zone's instrumental corrections using 35, 37 and 43 (δ) Virginis.

APPARATUS ON EVERY BLOCK (verified numerically; constants are mine but fitted from his numbers). Aberration is computed in Gauss's auxiliary-angle form, with ⊙ the Sun's longitude, ε ≈ 23°28' and k = 20.25".
- Define A sinΘ' = k sin⊙ and A cosΘ' = k cos⊙ cosε.
- In right ascension (arc): Δα_ab = −A cos(α−Θ') secδ.
- In declination: Δδ_ab = A sin(Θ'−α) sinδ − k cos⊙ sinε cosδ.
- For ⊙ = 1s1°27' = 31°27' (1796): Θ' = 33°42', log A = 1.2799n (A = 19.05).
- For ⊙ = 0s18°8' (8 Apr 1815): Θ' = 19°39', log A = 1.2730n (A = 18.75).

Nutation, with Ω the lunar node:
- Δα_nut = −16.54" sinΩ − B cos(α−δ') tanδ.
- Δδ_nut = −B sin(α−δ') (with his sign marks).
- Here B sinδ' ≈ 18.0" sinε sinΩ and B cosδ' ≈ −9.6" cosΩ. These are fitted constants: about 18.0" in longitude and 9.6" in obliquity.
- For Ω = 3s14°45' (1796): δ' = 109°29', log B = 0.8673n, constant RA term 16.00.
- For Ω = 3s7°59' (1815): δ' = 100°40', log B = 0.8596n, constant RA term 16.38.

Each block has four log columns, arranged as log A + log cos(α−Θ') + log secδ, and so on:
- column 1 gives the RA aberration;
- column 2 gives the declination aberration (variable part);
- column 3 gives the RA nutation tanδ term;
- column 4 gives the declination nutation.

BLOCK 1: δ Virginis.
- Start: catalogue mean place 191°22'57.90", +4°29'16.20". This is apparently Piazzi 1800.
- Step back 3.699 yr to 1796.301 (margin: log 3.699 = 0.56808).
- The annual rates are 45.08"/yr in RA (log 1.65398; includes proper motion) and 19.70"/yr in declination (log 1.29425).
- This gives −2'46.75" and +1'12.87", hence the 1796.301 mean place 191°20'11.15", +4°30'29.07".
- Add the 1796 aberration (+17.67, +0.57), the constant declination aberration (−6.84), and nutation (−16.00, −0.08; +7.29).
- Result: apparent place 191°20'12.74" = 12h45m20.85s, +4°30'30.09". This is the catalogue value against which the zone correction +0.14s on the previous page was formed.

BLOCKS 2 and 3: stars *a and *b.
- Lalande's 1796 apparent places are 190°32'36.15", +3°3'14.55" (a) and 190°37'17.40", +3°13'38.91" (b).
- (i) Remove the 1796 aberration and nutation (signs reversed), giving mean 1796.301 places.
- (ii) Precess over t = 1815.268 − 1796.301 = 18.967 yr (log 1.27800), with n = 20.06" (log 1.30242) and m t = 14'33.24" (log m ≈ 1.66313):
  - RA: Δα = m t + n t sinα_m tanδ_m.
  - Declination: Δδ = n t cosα_m.
  - Here α_m and δ_m are the mid-epoch values, e.g. α_m ≈ 190°40' for a.
  - Margin for a: 2.58042 = log(n t); 9.99244 = log|cos α_m|; 9.26728 = log|sin α_m|; 8.71967 = log tanδ_m. This gives −3.69" and −6'14.00".
  - Margin for b: 9.99232, 9.27041, 8.74410. This gives −3.94" and −6'13.89".
- (iii) Add the 1815 aberration and nutation:
  - a: +18.55, −16.38, 0 (RA); +0.15, −3.90, −3.77, +7.24 (declination).
  - b: +18.56, −16.38, 0 (RA); +0.16, −3.90, −3.76, +7.24 (declination).
  - The bracketed pair −3.90/−3.77 sums to −7.67. This matches the constant aberration term −k cos⊙ sinε cosδ ≈ −7.65". Why it is split into two parts is not clear to me.
- Results (apparent 1815.268): a = 190°47'6.39", +2°56'59.46"; b = 190°51'47.39", +3°7'23.93".

JUNO, 8 April 1815.
- RA from a: 190°34'52.74" at 10h44m7.0s, weight 9.
- RA from b: 190°34'50.39" at 10h47m13.1s, weight 5.
- Weighted means: time 10h45m13.5s, RA 190°34'51.90".
- Declination observed at 10h42m33.4s: 2°53'23.33". Reduced by Juno's motion (+0.85") to the same time, giving 2°53'24.18".

LALANDE ZONES OF 19 AND 21 FEBRUARY 1790 (new section).
- Transit times on 19 and 21 Feb:
  - 15 UMa: 8h54m0.17s / 8h54m29.17s.
  - 25: 9h18m45.10s / 9h19m14.43s.
  - 219 Bode: 10h57m5.77s / 10h57m35.18s.
- The two-day clock gains are 29.00, 29.33 and 29.41s, mean 29.25s. The rate factor is (1 − 1/2955)/2, i.e. 1 − 1/5910 per unit interval.
- 219 follows 15 by 2h3m5.60s and 2h3m6.01s, mean 2h3m5.805s. Times the rate factor this gives 2h3m4.56s.
- 219 follows 25 by 1h38m20.67s and 1h38m20.75s, mean 1h38m20.710s, giving 1h38m19.71s.
- From the zone readings (3°35'2", 3°46'13"/6" against 3°39'28"/21"), 15 is 4'22.50" north of 219 and 25 is 6'45.00" south of 219. These are the values used on the next page.

WIRE REDUCTION (last wire to middle).
- From Polaris: 801.33 s = 798.67 + 2.67.
- 801.33 × cos δ_Polaris (log 2.90381 + 8.49426) = 25.01 s, the equatorial wire interval.
- Divided by cos 52.5° (log 9.78439) this gives 41.08 s for stars at δ ≈ 52°30'. These are the I/II/III wire corrections (−41.08, +0.14, +40.94).

RIGHT COLUMN.
- Mean zone reading of 219 Bode: 3°39'24".
- Plus the zone constant 48°50'58" gives δ ≈ 52°30'22", i.e. 37°29'38" from the pole.
- Also 42°56'20" + 48°50'58" = 91°47'18".
errors: No substantive arithmetic error found. All additions and subtractions in the δ Vir, *a, *b and Juno blocks check to 0.01".

The 1815 constant declination aberration appears as two terms (−3.90, −3.77/−3.76) summing to −7.67. My recomputation gives −7.645". The difference is within the precision of his constants; the reason for the split is unclear.

'Gang der Uhr in 2 Tagen … (1 − 1/2955)': 29.25 s in 2 days is 1/5908 per unit time. The factor must be read as divided by 2, and this is confirmed by the result 2h3m5.805s → 2h3m4.56s. Not an error, but easy to misread.

results.usually_credited_to: Bradley; tabular forms by Gauss, Bessel, Zach (c. 1800–1830)

results.what: Weighted mean of Juno RA from two comparison stars (weights 9 and 5) and reduction of declination to common time
Re-reduction of Lalande Histoire Céleste zones (clock rate from repeated transits, wire-interval reduction via cos δ)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine positional-astronomy reductions (precession, aberration, nutation, clock rate, wire intervals) of the kind Gauss performed constantly for minor-planet work. There is no new mathematics.

transcription_corrections: Left margin '1.66717' is almost certainly '1.66313' (log m; 1.27800 + 1.66313 → 873.2" = 14'33.24"; the next page also has 1.66313).
'78439' is the logarithm 9.78439 = log cos 52°30', used as a divisor.
The rate factor reads (1 − 1/2955) with a '2' beneath, i.e. halved per two days, giving 1/5910.
'Θ 0.18.8' and 'δ 3.7.59' on the *a line are the Sun's longitude 0s18°8' and the lunar node ☊ 3s7°59' for 8 April 1815. The 'δ'' entries are the nutation auxiliary angle, not a declination.
